subject: Capture boundary worked examples: session tokens, prompts, and derivative artifacts
messages:

Cc: procurement@brightbank.com

Subject: Questions on what Redwood keeps by default (worked examples)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and security asked for a short worked-example doc that shows what Redwood stores by default vs what is ephemeral, using realistic cases from our planned integration. Specifically they'd like answers for: streaming sessions (token-by-token), file attachments uploaded as part of a request, prompts that include PII, generated summaries/artifacts, and embeddings.

We attached a short questionnaire and scope doc — see attachments. Can you confirm:
- Which items are retained by default and for how long?
- How to submit a deletion/erasure request for a single session vs entire account?
- Residency: if we select eu-west region, are logs and stored derivatives kept in-region?

Appreciate concrete examples (e.g., "Customer query X -> request stored for N days; streaming tokens discarded after T hours; derived summary kept for M days unless customer opts out").

Best,
Anita Singh
BrightBank — Senior Procurement Manager

Attachments: brightbank-questionnaire.pdf

From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: A. Singh <asingh@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-15T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood keeps by default (worked examples)

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. See worked examples below; I kept bullets short so procurement can paste into their attachment. I also linked our public residency page and opened a support ticket for SOC 2 artifacts (SUP-9482).

Summary (short):
- Request/response (text inputs and model outputs): hosted API: default retention 30 days for telemetry and full request/response logs. After 30 days logs are purged from hot store and retained for an additional 60 days in encrypted cold archive for incident investigations, then deleted (total horizon 90 days) unless a customer opts in to extended retention.
- Streaming tokens (in-flight): transient. Token-by-token buffers are kept for up to 2 hours to support reconnection and partial replay; not indexed and not included in analytics by default.
- Prompts containing PII: treated as requests. They are included in the 30-day window above; customers can opt-in to have requests excluded from telemetry retention with an account-level flag or use our private deployment.
- Generated derivatives (summaries, extracted metadata): classified as "derived outputs." By default they are retained for 90 days and may be surfaced in usage analytics; customers can configure shorter retention or automatic purging for derivatives via the Console (per-route policy).
- Embeddings and vectors: not stored by default unless the customer explicitly enables vector indexing or calls the embeddings persistence API. If enabled they follow the embedding index retention settings (default 365 days) and can be scoped to region/residency.
- File attachments uploaded as part of a request (e.g., transcripts, PDFs): stored as artifacts attached to the request. Default retention aligns with request logs (30/90 day pattern). Attachments marked sensitive can be flagged for expedited purge.

Worked examples (pasteable):
1) Single user chat (hosted API, us region): user sends prompt with name and address; model returns a short answer. Request + full answer stored for 30 days; streaming tokens kept invisible and transient (<=2 hours). To remove that single session: submit a deletion request via Console > Data & Privacy > Erase session (or file SUP-9482 for manual erasure if immediate).
2) Streaming transcription (long-running connection): audio streamed -> tokens buffered for reconnection up to 2 hours; at finalization the full transcript is stored as the request and follows 30-day retention.
3) Customer runs auto-summary job that generates a "meeting-summary" artifact: summary considered derived output and kept for 90 days by default; you can enable per-route purge to have it deleted after 7 days.
4) Embedding index for search (optional): embedding vectors stored only if you call the persistent embeddings API; default index TTL is 365 days unless retention policy changed by account admin.

Residency note: If you pick eu-west as the deployment region we persist request logs and stored derivatives in-region by default. Cold archival copies for legal hold can be scoped to region on request — we'll need a contract clause for long-term on-shore archiving.

How to request deletion:
- Self-serve (recommended): Console > Data & Privacy > Erase session / Erase account exports. This triggers automated workflow and provides a confirmation ID.
- Manual/legal: open a support ticket and include the confirmation ID; for account-wide erasures we'll coordinate with Security and Engineering; typical SLA 5 business days for hosted tenants.

Next steps: I can (a) produce a 1-page table mapping "example -> what is stored by default -> retention horizon -> how to erase" for procurement, (b) loop Security to provide SOC 2 artifact references. Let me know which you want first.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

2) SOC 2 artifacts: procurement will need the Type II report and the list of controls mapped to our security questionnaire. Can Security/Compliance provide those items under an NDA?

Can you also confirm the self-serve erase workflow returns an audit id we can consume programmatically? If so, procurement will include that as a required integration point.

Appreciate it — please also include the 1-page table you mentioned.

Anita
